summary.text: Alex Breskin is the Greens candidate for Mordialloc at the 2026 Victorian election. A software developer who lives in Mordialloc, he has held several posts with the Kingston Residents Association. He has stood for the Greens many times, including in Mordialloc in 2014, Isaacs in 2016 and 2022, at the head of the party's South-Eastern Metropolitan ticket in 2022 and at the 2024 Dunkley by-election.

prior_roles.role: Treasurer, Vice President and Acting President
prior_roles.note: His page lists these posts without years; it does not say whether any is current
The ABC gives this post; his own page lists other posts at the association and names him secretary of Residents Against Mordialloc Freeway instead

priorities.text: Stronger climate action to protect local waterways and wildlife
More public housing that people in need can get into

summary.text: Lily Potucek is the Family First candidate for Mordialloc at the 2026 Victorian election; the ABC guide first listed her as Potecuk and now uses the party's spelling. On the party's website she says she is a Melbourne-born nurse who also holds a business degree, and that she and her husband have four children. The ABC's guide lists her without a biography.

priorities.text: Protecting free speech and religious expression
Action on crime and youth offending
Repairing potholes and neglected local roads
Less government bureaucracy and opposition to digital control measures
Restricting late-term abortion and more support for women in difficult pregnancies

sources.title: Mordialloc: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Lily Potucek, Candidate for Mordialloc, Family First Party Australia

summary.text: Mahee Hossain is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Mordialloc at the 2026 Victorian election. Born in Dandenong, he is a software engineer at NAB and a workplace delegate for the Finance Sector Union. He describes years of activism on climate change, anti-racism, community health clinic closures and Palestine.

priorities.text: Tackling the housing shortage and cost of living by redistributing wealth from the rich
Rebuilding the capacity of working people to organise and fight back
Opposing the closure of community health clinics

sources.title: Mordialloc: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Mahee Hossain, Victorian Socialists

summary.text: Nadia Ticehurst is the One Nation candidate for Mordialloc at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC's guide says she has nursed in critical care and operating theatres in the public system for 26 years, was born in Melbourne's east, and has competed for Australia at Half Ironman triathlon world championships. One Nation's candidate page could not be read (it refuses automated requests), and we found no other published biography as at early November 2026.

occupation.text: Critical care and operating suite nurse

sources.title: Mordialloc: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Paul O'Halloran is the Liberal candidate for Mordialloc at the 2026 Victorian election. He has spent more than four decades in Victoria Police, including time as a homicide detective and as an acting assistant commissioner, and became a commander in Crime Command in 2021, the year he received the Australian Police Medal. He grew up in Mordialloc.

priorities.text: Reducing crime, including drug use in the community
Lowering living costs for local families

sources.title: Mordialloc: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Paul O'Halloran, Liberal for Mordialloc, Liberal Victoria

summary.text: Rachel Versteegen is the Libertarian candidate for Mordialloc at the 2026 Victorian election. She was second on the Liberal Democrats' Northern Metropolitan upper-house ticket in 2022 and stood for the renamed Libertarian Party in the federal seat of Wills in 2025. Neither the ABC nor the party had published a biography as at early November 2026, and she was not yet on the Victorian Libertarians' candidate page.

previous_candidacies.note: Second on the Liberal Democrats ticket; the party is now the Libertarian Party

sources.title: Mordialloc: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Results of the 2022 Victorian state election (Legislative Council), Wikipedia
Results of the 2025 Australian federal election in Victoria, Wikipedia

summary.text: Renee Thompson is the Legalise Cannabis Victoria candidate for Mordialloc at the 2026 Victorian election, on the VEC's list of nominations. According to the ABC's guide she works as a marriage celebrant and event producer and had until recently been employed by local government in community development. She was the party's candidate at the Nepean by-election in May 2026, where she won 2.9 per cent of first preferences.

prior_roles.note: The ABC says she held the role until recently; it does not name the council.

sources.title: Candidates for Mordialloc District, Victorian Electoral Commission
Mordialloc, 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
2026 Nepean state by-election, Wikipedia

summary.text: Tim Richardson has been Labor's member for Mordialloc since 2014, and was re-elected in 2018 and 2022. In August 2026 he became Minister for Local Government, Consumer Affairs and Renters, having been Cabinet Secretary from April 2026 and a parliamentary secretary in several portfolios before that. He previously worked as an adviser to state and federal governments. He is recontesting Mordialloc in 2026.

occupation.text: Adviser in state and federal governments

prior_roles.role: Parliamentary Secretary for Men's Behaviour Change (later also Health and Wellbeing)
Parliamentary Secretary for Mental Health and Suicide Prevention
Parliamentary Secretary for Mental Health and Social Inclusion
prior_roles.note: The Parliament of Victoria page dates this from June 2022; Wikipedia dates it from June 2018.

prior_roles.role: Chair, Public Accounts and Estimates Committee
Adviser in state and federal governments
prior_roles.note: The Parliament biography gives no years.

faction.name: Labor Left
faction.note: Wikipedia says he moved from Labor Right to Labor Left soon after the 2022 election.

priorities.text: More investment in education, from kindergarten to school upgrades and inclusive schooling
Easier access to mental health support
Recognising First Nations people through a treaty
